observation: Fresh main still treated expectedSha256 as a truthy optional value and coerced it with String(). Explicit empty/false values silently removed the preimage guard, while numeric or malformed strings survived federation and were only rejected later by ChangesetStore preimage comparison. That allowed candidate selection to trust a validation plan whose concurrency assertion had already been weakened or malformed.
changes: Treat presence of expectedSha256 as an explicit preimage assertion and require it to already be a lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 string.
Reject a malformed expectedSha256 through the existing invalid-change fail-closed path instead of omitting or coercing it.
Preserve valid lower-case SHA-256 assertions exactly so existing consensus fingerprints and downstream PREIMAGE_MISMATCH behavior remain unchanged.

verification.pre_fix_source_contract_replay: EXPECTED FAIL: ...(c.expectedSha256?{expectedSha256:String(c.expectedSha256)}:{}) silently omitted falsey explicit assertions and coerced truthy malformed values.
verification.downstream_contract_evidence: ChangesetStore already uses /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/ for durable hashes and compares supplied expectedSha256 exactly against the observed preimage SHA-256; this cycle aligns federation with that existing reality.
verification.focused_regression_contract: tests/federated-preimage-shape-integrity.test.mjs covers empty, boolean/numeric, uppercase and malformed hashes, preserves a valid lowercase hash, and proves malformed candidates cannot win over a valid guarded alternative.
verification.hosted_runtime: Developer Execution Runtime remained temporarily unavailable with HTTP 502; no hosted full-suite pass is claimed.

truth_boundary: This cycle does not invent a new concurrency mechanism. It only prevents federation from weakening the existing expectedSha256 preimage assertion before ChangeSet staging.
